title: Neuromuscular Disorders — DMD, SMA, Neuropathies & NMJ

calc_items.title: IVIg daily dose
calc_items.question: An 18-kg child with GBS receives IVIg 0.4 g/kg/day for five days. What is the daily amount and the total course?

calc_items.title: IVIg volume
calc_items.question: A 5% IVIg solution contains 5 g/100 mL. What volume delivers 7.2 g?

calc_items.title: X-linked recurrence (son)
calc_items.question: A DMD carrier mother and an unaffected father are expecting a boy. What is the probability that this son is affected?
calc_items.working: Each son has a 1/2 chance of inheriting the variant X = 50%.

calc_items.title: Autosomal recessive recurrence
calc_items.question: Both parents are SMA carriers. What is the probability that a child is affected?

calc_items.title: Glucocorticoid dose arithmetic
calc_items.question: A 24-kg boy with DMD is on a steroid at 0.75 mg/kg/day. Calculate the daily dose. (Arithmetic only, not a prescription.)
calc_items.working: 0.75 × 24 = 18 mg/day; example calculation only, not a prescription.

calc_items.title: IVIg total course
calc_items.question: A 25-kg child is to receive IVIg 2 g/kg in total. How many grams is that?

calc_items.title: IVIg daily share
calc_items.question: A child receives 50 g of IVIg divided equally over 5 days. How much per day?

calc_items.title: SMN2 copy difference
calc_items.question: One child with SMA has 2 SMN2 copies and another has 4. What is the absolute difference in copy number?
calc_items.working: 4 − 2 = 2 copies; phenotype prediction from copy number is not deterministic.

added_why_not.Anti-AChR antibody testing: AChR antibodies test for autoimmune myasthenia gravis; a very high CK with calf pseudohypertrophy points to a dystrophinopathy.
added_why_not.Muscle biopsy as first test in every chi: Genetic testing is first-line; biopsy is kept for cases where genetic testing is inconclusive.
added_why_not.SMN1 exon 7 copy-number analysis: SMN1 testing confirms SMA, which has a normal or mildly raised CK and no pseudohypertrophy.
added_why_not.Deletion of SMN1 with SMN2 modifier: That describes 5q SMA, not a dystrophin nonsense variant.
added_why_not.Expansion of DMPK CTG repeats: DMPK CTG expansion causes myotonic dystrophy type 1.
added_why_not.Stable in-frame internally shortened dys: That is the Becker mechanism; a nonsense variant creates a premature stop codon and absent dystrophin.
added_why_not.Out-of-frame frameshift with absent dyst: Out-of-frame variants with absent dystrophin typically cause Duchenne, the more severe form.
added_why_not.Biallelic SMN1 loss: Biallelic SMN1 loss causes SMA, not a dystrophinopathy.
added_why_not.Maternal mitochondrial heteroplasmy: Dystrophinopathies are X-linked; heteroplasmy concerns mitochondrial DNA disorders.
added_why_not.Primary cerebellar ataxia: Ataxia causes incoordination; climbing up the thighs reflects proximal hip-girdle weakness.
added_why_not.Distal sensory neuropathy: Neuropathy causes distal weakness and sensory loss; the Gowers sign reflects proximal weakness.
added_why_not.Neuromuscular fatigability confined to e: Ocular myasthenia causes ptosis and diplopia, not proximal hip weakness.
added_why_not.Pure autonomic neuropathy: Autonomic neuropathy does not cause a CK of about 20,000 U/L or proximal weakness.
added_why_not.Acquired demyelinating polyneuropathy: Demyelinating neuropathy slows nerve conduction; normal NCS with very high CK indicates myopathy.
added_why_not.Anterior horn cell disease confirmed by: SMA shows reduced CMAP amplitudes and a normal or mildly raised CK, not CK 20,000; normal NCS does not confirm it.
added_why_not.Half of sons and half of daughters: A father passes his X to every daughter and his Y to every son.
added_why_not.Only children with high SMN2 copy number: SMN2 copy number concerns SMA, not X-linked transmission.
added_why_not.All sons and none of his daughters: Sons receive their father's Y chromosome, so they cannot inherit his X-linked variant.
added_why_not.25% chance of inheriting the variant: 25% is the risk for any child of being an affected son; for a son specifically it is 50%.
added_why_not.100% chance of inheriting the variant: A heterozygous carrier mother passes the variant X to half her children, not all.
added_why_not.0% chance of inheriting the variant: A carrier mother can pass the variant X to her sons.
added_why_not.Routine systemic antibiotics: Antibiotics treat infection; they have no effect on dystrophic muscle decline.
added_why_not.Long-term pyridostigmine as the primary: Pyridostigmine treats myasthenia; it does not slow DMD progression.
added_why_not.Repeated IVIg courses: IVIg treats immune-mediated neuropathy or myasthenia; DMD is not autoimmune.
added_why_not.CK reflects left ventricular ejection fr: CK reflects skeletal muscle breakdown and falls as muscle is lost; it does not measure cardiac function.
added_why_not.Cardiac involvement occurs only after lo: Cardiomyopathy can start while the child still walks; surveillance begins at diagnosis.
added_why_not.Normal ECG excludes future cardiomyopath: A normal ECG does not exclude evolving fibrosis; echo or cardiac MRI surveillance continues.
added_why_not.Thyroid storm: Morning headache and fatigue in advanced DMD point to nocturnal hypoventilation, not thyroid disease.
added_why_not.Central diabetes insipidus: Diabetes insipidus causes polyuria and polydipsia, not morning headaches from CO₂ retention.
added_why_not.Isolated peripheral vestibulopathy: Vestibular disorders cause vertigo, not morning headache with fatigue.
added_why_not.Risk of cholinergic crisis: Cholinergic crisis comes from excess anticholinesterase in myasthenia, not from stopping steroids.
added_why_not.Risk of rebound hyperthyroidism: Stopping steroids does not cause hyperthyroidism; the risk is adrenal insufficiency.
added_why_not.Risk of sudden SMN2 exon skipping: SMN2 splicing concerns SMA therapy and is not affected by steroids.
added_why_not.Number of SMN2 copies only: SMN2 copy number guides SMA prognosis, not DMD exon-skipping eligibility.
added_why_not.Positive anti-MuSK antibody titre: MuSK antibodies relate to myasthenia gravis, not dystrophin exon skipping.
added_why_not.Presence of elevated CSF protein: Raised CSF protein suggests GBS or CIDP; it is irrelevant to exon-skipping eligibility.
added_why_not.Pure dysautonomia with normal muscle str: DMD causes marked proximal weakness, not isolated autonomic failure.
added_why_not.Length-dependent sensory loss preceding: That is neuropathy; DMD spares sensation.
added_why_not.Fluctuating diplopia isolated to evening: Fatigable diplopia suggests myasthenia, not a dystrophy.
added_why_not.Onion-bulb formations confined to periph: Onion bulbs are seen in nerve biopsy in demyelinating neuropathy (e.g. CMT1A).
added_why_not.Postsynaptic receptor loss with normal m: That describes myasthenia; dystrophinopathy shows necrosis, regeneration and absent dystrophin.
added_why_not.Grouped small angular fibres with normal: Grouped atrophy indicates neurogenic disease such as SMA, with normal dystrophin.
added_why_not.Immobilization without physiotherapy: Immobility worsens contractures; daily stretching and orthoses help preserve range.
added_why_not.Avoiding assessment until wheelchair dep: Contractures are prevented by early, regular assessment, not by waiting for wheelchair use.
added_why_not.Bed rest to prevent all muscle use: Bed rest accelerates weakness and contractures in DMD.
added_why_not.Serum acetylcholine receptor antibody: AChR antibodies are markers of myasthenia, not muscular dystrophy.
added_why_not.CSF oligoclonal bands: Oligoclonal bands suggest CNS inflammation such as MS, not dystrophy.
added_why_not.Plasma copper concentration: Copper is relevant to Wilson and Menkes disease, not DMD.
added_why_not.Autosomal recessive with SMN1 biallelic: That is SMA inheritance; dystrophinopathies are X-linked.
added_why_not.Autosomal dominant with full penetrance: Dystrophinopathies are X-linked recessive, affecting mainly males.
added_why_not.Mitochondrial maternal inheritance: Mitochondrial inheritance affects both sexes via the mother; DMD is X-linked.
added_why_not.Only weekly visual acuity measurement: DMD does not mainly affect vision; heart, lungs, spine and bone need surveillance.
added_why_not.Stop cardiology visits after wheelchair: Cardiac risk increases after loss of ambulation; surveillance must continue.
added_why_not.Only muscle CK serial monitoring: CK falls as muscle is lost and does not track cardiac, respiratory or spinal complications.
added_why_not.Adenomatous polyposis: Polyposis is unrelated to steroids or DMD; back pain on steroids suggests a vertebral fracture.
added_why_not.Optic neuritis: Optic neuritis causes visual loss with painful eye movements, not vertebral pain.
added_why_not.Acute inflammatory demyelinating neuropa: GBS causes ascending weakness and areflexia; vertebral pain on chronic steroids suggests a fragility fracture.
added_why_not.All affected boys must have affected fat: DMD is X-linked; fathers pass a Y to sons, so affected boys inherit the variant from their mothers or de novo.
added_why_not.A normal maternal CK excludes carrier st: Carrier CK is normal in many carriers; genetic testing is required.
added_why_not.Daughters of affected fathers never inhe: An affected father passes his X to every daughter, so all are obligate carriers.
added_why_not.Synovial proliferation within the knee: Pseudohypertrophy is in the calf muscle, not the knee joint.
added_why_not.Increase in contractile muscle fibres al: True hypertrophy would increase strength; in DMD fat and fibrosis replace muscle.
added_why_not.Peripheral oedema from kidney failure: Oedema is soft and pitting; DMD calves are firm because of fibro-fatty replacement.
added_why_not.Routine plasma exchange: Plasma exchange removes antibodies (GBS, myasthenia); it does not help DMD respiratory weakness.
added_why_not.Peripheral nerve decompression: Weak cough in DMD comes from respiratory muscle weakness, not nerve entrapment.
added_why_not.Long-term anti-epileptic monotherapy: Antiseizure drugs do not treat respiratory muscle weakness.
added_why_not.Preschool Gowers and dystrophin deletion: These are DMD features and do not separate it from myotonic dystrophy.
added_why_not.X-linked pedigree with high CK: That pattern supports DMD; congenital myotonic dystrophy is autosomal dominant with maternal transmission.
added_why_not.Absent dystrophin immunostaining: Absent dystrophin confirms DMD; dystrophin is normal in myotonic dystrophy.
added_why_not.CK level uniquely predicts exon amenabil: Exon amenability depends on the specific deletion, not on CK.
added_why_not.CK excludes cardiac risk: CK does not reflect cardiac involvement.
added_why_not.CK alone determines glucocorticoid stres: Stress dosing depends on steroid exposure and the procedure or illness, not on CK.
added_why_not.Treat all dysphagia as conversion disord: Late DMD dysphagia is organic (oropharyngeal weakness) and risks aspiration.
added_why_not.Serum anti-AChR alone as definitive DMD: AChR antibodies are irrelevant in DMD.
added_why_not.Eliminate respiratory surveillance: Dysphagia raises aspiration risk, so respiratory surveillance becomes more important.
added_why_not.Primary corticospinal tract disease: Upper motor neuron disease gives hyperreflexia, not areflexia with tongue fasciculations.
added_why_not.Peripheral sensory neuronopathy: Sensory neuronopathy causes sensory ataxia, not fasciculations with profound weakness.
added_why_not.Neuromuscular junction autoimmune blocka: NMJ disorders give fatigable weakness without fasciculations or areflexia.
added_why_not.DMD exon deletion on Xp21: Xp21 deletions cause Duchenne/Becker, not SMA.
added_why_not.CTG expansion in DMPK: DMPK CTG expansion causes myotonic dystrophy type 1.
added_why_not.Lower SMN2 copy number in every case: Fewer SMN2 copies predict a more severe phenotype, not a milder one.
added_why_not.Higher DMD copy number: DMD gene copies are unrelated to SMA severity.
added_why_not.Positive anti-AChR antibodies: AChR antibodies indicate myasthenia and do not modify SMA.
added_why_not.Dystrophin exon 51 skipping: Exon 51 skipping (eteplirsen) is a DMD therapy.
added_why_not.AAV delivery of an SMN1 transgene: That is onasemnogene abeparvovec (gene therapy), not nusinersen.
added_why_not.Small-molecule SMN2 splicing taken orall: That is risdiplam; nusinersen is an intrathecal antisense oligonucleotide.
added_why_not.Intravenous single infusion: A single IV infusion describes onasemnogene; nusinersen is given intrathecally.
added_why_not.Intrathecal SMN1 antisense oligonucleoti: Nusinersen is an intrathecal ASO acting on SMN2; risdiplam is oral.
added_why_not.Intravenous dystrophin replacement: No such therapy exists, and dystrophin is irrelevant to SMA.
added_why_not.Neutralization of acetylcholine receptor: This is the myasthenia mechanism, not SMA gene therapy.
added_why_not.Makes genotype confirmation unnecessary: A positive screen still needs confirmatory SMN1/SMN2 testing.
added_why_not.Reverses all lost motor neurons regardle: Lost motor neurons do not regenerate; that is why early treatment matters.
added_why_not.Eliminates the need for multidisciplinar: Treated children still need respiratory, nutritional and orthopaedic care.
added_why_not.Isolated upper-airway structural stenosi: Upper-airway stenosis causes stridor, not a bell-shaped chest with paradoxical breathing.
added_why_not.Isolated cardiomyopathy: SMA does not cause cardiomyopathy; the chest shape reflects intercostal weakness.
added_why_not.Severe primary diaphragmatic paralysis w: In SMA the diaphragm is relatively spared and the intercostals are weak — the reverse.
added_why_not.Routine high-dose sedatives: Sedatives depress respiratory drive in children with weak respiratory muscles.
added_why_not.Cease infection prevention: Vaccination and infection prevention are key in weak-cough SMA.
added_why_not.Obtain lumbar puncture at every visit: Lumbar puncture is for nusinersen dosing, not routine respiratory care.
added_why_not.Independent walking achieved in infancy: Independent walking defines SMA type 3, not type 1.
added_why_not.Normal adult ambulation: Type 1 children never sit unaided; adult ambulation describes type 4.
added_why_not.Only distal hand weakness after puberty: SMA is proximal-predominant; type 1 presents in early infancy.
added_why_not.Never achieves independent head control: That describes type 1; type 2 children sit independently.
added_why_not.Always walks independently: Independent walking defines type 3, not type 2.
added_why_not.Severe prenatal contractures in all pati: Prenatal onset with contractures is type 0; type 3 children walk.
added_why_not.50% for each son but none of daughters: That is an X-linked pattern; SMA is autosomal recessive.
added_why_not.100% of pregnancies: Two carriers have a 25% risk in each pregnancy.
added_why_not.0% if the first child survived: Recurrence risk is independent of a sibling's outcome.
added_why_not.DMD immunohistochemistry alone: Dystrophin staining evaluates dystrophinopathy, not SMA.
added_why_not.Only CSF oligoclonal band testing: Oligoclonal bands are for CNS inflammation.
added_why_not.Feeding tests determine DMD exon positio: Swallow assessment has no link to DMD genetics.
added_why_not.Treatment eliminates all dysphagia risk: Bulbar weakness may persist or progress despite treatment.
added_why_not.Aspiration cannot occur without fever: Silent aspiration is common and often afebrile.
added_why_not.Only lens opacity: Lens opacity is not a recognised onasemnogene toxicity; the liver and platelets are monitored.
added_why_not.Only peripheral neuropathy: Neuropathy is not the main toxicity; hepatotoxicity and thrombocytopenia (and TMA) are.
added_why_not.Selective nephrotic syndrome as the sole: Renal TMA can occur, but liver injury and thrombocytopenia are the key monitored effects.
added_why_not.Marked calf pseudohypertrophy and classi: These are DMD features, not SMA.
added_why_not.Primary distal sensory loss: Both SMA and DMD spare sensation.
added_why_not.Delay until motor milestones are lost: Delay allows irreversible motor-neuron loss; presymptomatic therapy is best.
added_why_not.Use creatine kinase alone to confirm SMA: CK is normal or mildly raised in SMA; genetic confirmation is needed.
added_why_not.Wait until independent walking age: Delay loses the presymptomatic treatment window.
added_why_not.Juvenile myasthenia gravis: Myasthenia causes fatigable ocular/bulbar weakness with preserved reflexes.
added_why_not.Duchenne muscular dystrophy: DMD is slowly progressive proximal weakness, not acute post-infectious paralysis.
added_why_not.Spinal muscular atrophy type 1: SMA type 1 presents in early infancy, not after diarrhoea in a previously normal child.
added_why_not.Begin long-term oral steroids as sole th: Steroids are ineffective in GBS; monitoring and IVIg or plasma exchange are needed.
added_why_not.Discharge because weakness is symmetrica: Symmetrical rapidly progressive weakness is typical of GBS and needs admission.
added_why_not.Wait for CSF protein rise before monitor: CSF protein may be normal early; monitoring cannot wait.
added_why_not.Normal protein excludes GBS at any time: Albuminocytological dissociation often appears only after the first week.
added_why_not.Normal protein establishes SMA: CSF protein does not diagnose SMA.
added_why_not.Normal CSF mandates a primary myopathy d: A normal early CSF does not point to myopathy.
added_why_not.Long-course oral prednisolone alone: Oral steroids are not effective in GBS.
added_why_not.Exon-skipping dystrophin treatment: Exon skipping is a DMD therapy.
added_why_not.Systemic corticosteroids alone: Steroids alone have not been shown to help GBS.
added_why_not.Acetazolamide: Acetazolamide is used for periodic paralysis and IIH, not GBS.
added_why_not.Dystrophinopathy only: Dystrophinopathy is a slowly progressive myopathy, not a relapsing neuropathy.
added_why_not.Congenital myasthenic syndrome only: CMS is a congenital NMJ disorder, not an acquired relapsing neuropathy.
added_why_not.Persistent simple Bell palsy: Bell palsy is an isolated facial nerve palsy.
added_why_not.AMAN without cranial features: AMAN is pure motor axonal GBS without ophthalmoplegia or ataxia.
added_why_not.Pure sensory small-fibre neuropathy: Small-fibre neuropathy causes pain and dysautonomia, not ophthalmoplegia and ataxia.
added_why_not.DMD carrier phenotype: DMD carriers do not develop ophthalmoplegia, ataxia and areflexia.
added_why_not.Direct quantification of dystrophin prot: Dystrophin is measured on muscle biopsy, not by nerve conduction.
added_why_not.SMN2 copy number: SMN2 copies are measured by genetic testing.
added_why_not.Neuromuscular junction antibody titre: Antibodies are serological tests, not electrophysiology.
added_why_not.Juvenile ocular myasthenia: Ocular myasthenia causes ptosis and diplopia, not distal wasting with pes cavus.
added_why_not.Acute GBS: GBS is acute; a familial, chronic distal neuropathy with pes cavus is CMT.
added_why_not.Congenital muscular dystrophy in all cas: CMD is a myopathy with high CK, not a familial distal neuropathy.
added_why_not.DMD from dystrophin out-of-frame variant: DMD is a myopathy with normal nerve conduction.
added_why_not.Congenital myotonic dystrophy: Myotonic dystrophy is a myopathy and does not uniformly slow conduction.
added_why_not.5q SMA from SMN1 deletion: SMA affects motor neurons with normal sensory conduction.
added_why_not.Pure primary cerebellar lesion: Cerebellar lesions do not cause areflexia and reduced vibration with pes cavus.
added_why_not.Primary junction disorder with normal se: NMJ disorders preserve sensation and reflexes.
added_why_not.Generalized dystrophin deficiency: Dystrophin deficiency causes generalised myopathy, not focal wrist drop.
added_why_not.Autoimmune generalized myasthenia: Myasthenia causes fatigable generalised weakness, not focal compressive wrist drop.
added_why_not.Congenital dystrophinopathy: Dystrophinopathy is not post-infectious or acute.
added_why_not.Demyelinating CMT1A: CMT1A is an inherited chronic neuropathy.
added_why_not.Ocular myasthenia: Ocular myasthenia is not ascending areflexic paralysis.
added_why_not.Pain confirms pure central demyelination: Pain in GBS is radicular or neuropathic, not evidence of central demyelination.
added_why_not.Pain excludes GBS: Back and limb pain is common in childhood GBS and can precede weakness.
added_why_not.Preserved normal CK: CK is usually normal in GBS and does not guide acuity.
added_why_not.Normal vision: Vision does not predict respiratory failure.
added_why_not.No family history of neuropathy: Family history is irrelevant to acute GBS deterioration.
added_why_not.Anterior horn cell: Anterior horn cell disease causes fasciculations and areflexia, not fatigable ptosis.
added_why_not.Corticospinal tract: UMN lesions cause spasticity and hyperreflexia, not fluctuating ptosis.
added_why_not.Primary length-dependent sensory nerve: Sensory neuropathy does not cause fatigable ptosis and diplopia.
added_why_not.PMP22 antibody: PMP22 is a gene (CMT1A), not an autoantibody target.
added_why_not.Anti-GQ1b as sole test: Anti-GQ1b supports Miller Fisher syndrome, not myasthenia.
added_why_not.Anti-dystrophin antibody: There is no autoimmune anti-dystrophin test for myasthenia.
added_why_not.Anti-insulin receptor antibody: This relates to severe insulin resistance syndromes.
added_why_not.Ambulatory outpatient observation: Bulbar and respiratory weakness is myasthenic crisis and needs emergency care.
added_why_not.Isolated exercise therapy: Exercise worsens fatigable weakness in crisis.
added_why_not.Delay until antibody results return: Crisis is treated immediately on clinical grounds.
added_why_not.Eteplirsen: Eteplirsen is a DMD exon-51-skipping drug.
added_why_not.CMT1A: CMT1A is an inherited demyelinating neuropathy, not a junction disorder.
added_why_not.Acute inflammatory demyelinating GBS: GBS is acquired and post-infectious, not a congenital junction disorder.
added_why_not.Classic DMD: DMD is a myopathy, not a junction disorder.
added_why_not.All subtypes respond identically to acet: Some CMS subtypes (e.g. DOK7, slow-channel) worsen with pyridostigmine.
added_why_not.Antibodies predict every congenital subt: CMS is genetic and seronegative; subtype is defined by genetics.
added_why_not.CMT1A presenting as isolated ocular defi: CMT1A does not present with ptosis.
added_why_not.SMN1 deficiency: SMN1 deficiency is SMA, not a toxin.
added_why_not.AChR-blocking autoantibodies: That is autoimmune myasthenia, not botulism.
added_why_not.CIDP: CIDP is a chronic acquired neuropathy, not descending weakness with constipation in an infant.
added_why_not.Isolated absence epilepsy: Absence seizures are brief lapses of awareness, not hypotonia and weak suck.
added_why_not.DMD: DMD does not present in infancy with descending bulbar weakness and constipation.
added_why_not.Prominent length-dependent sensory impai: Sensory loss indicates neuropathy; NMJ disorders spare sensation.
added_why_not.Universal absent tendon reflexes: Absent reflexes suggest neuropathy such as GBS.
added_why_not.Marked CK rise above 10,000 U/L: Very high CK indicates myopathy, not NMJ disease.
added_why_not.Dystrophin exon skipping: Exon skipping is a DMD therapy with no role in myasthenic crisis.
added_why_not.Proximal weakness with CK 20,000 U/L: Very high CK with fixed proximal weakness indicates a myopathy, not fluctuating junction dysfunction.
added_why_not.Long-term anti-tubercular therapy: Anti-tubercular therapy has no role in myasthenic crisis.
added_why_not.Gradually progressive fixed distal senso: Fixed distal sensory loss is a neuropathy, not fluctuating NMJ dysfunction.
added_why_not.Postinfectious autoimmune neuropathy at: GBS does not occur at birth from maternal MG; transient neonatal MG does.
added_why_not.PMP22 duplication in all newborns: PMP22 duplication causes CMT1A, not transient neonatal weakness.
added_why_not.Inherited DMD variant from father's Y ch: DMD is X-linked; fathers pass a Y to sons.
added_why_not.Routine CSF protein testing every month: CSF protein has no role in scoliosis surveillance.
added_why_not.Serial acetylcholine receptor antibodies: AChR antibodies are irrelevant to SMA.
added_why_not.Only annual creatine kinase: CK does not monitor scoliosis or respiratory compromise.
added_why_not.Fixed splitting from ASD: ASD causes wide, fixed splitting that does not vary with respiration.
added_why_not.Paradoxical splitting from LBBB: In paradoxical splitting the interval narrows in inspiration and widens in expiration.
added_why_not.Wide splitting due to PS: PS delays P2, giving persistently wide splitting.
added_why_not.Elective catheter ASD device closure: Closing the atrial communication would worsen an obstructed TAPVC; the obstruction needs surgery.
added_why_not.Routine PGE1 as definitive therapy: PGE1 cannot relieve pulmonary venous obstruction and may worsen oedema.
added_why_not.Observe until pulmonary edema subsides: Obstructed TAPVC is a neonatal surgical emergency.
added_why_not.Exercise stress testing first: Hypotension with effusion after device closure suggests erosion with tamponade; exercise testing is dangerous.
added_why_not.Empirical antireflux therapy: Chest pain with hypotension and effusion is not reflux.
added_why_not.Apical muscular: Muscular VSDs are common in neonates but perimembranous defects are the most common overall.
added_why_not.Outlet supracristal: Supracristal VSDs are uncommon (more frequent in Asian populations).
added_why_not.Inlet septal: Inlet VSDs are typical of AV septal defects and uncommon in isolation.
added_why_not.Type B window: Type B is short and window-like.
added_why_not.Type C tubular: Type C is tubular, without constriction.
added_why_not.Type D complex: Type D has multiple constrictions; a funnel with an aortic ampulla is type A.
added_why_not.Isolated pulmonary venous obstruction: Pulmonary venous obstruction is unrelated to the LVOT shape in AVSD.
added_why_not.Fixed supravalvar aortic stenosis: Supravalvar AS is above the valve (e.g. Williams syndrome), not the elongated LVOT of AVSD.
added_why_not.Complete AVSD with common valve: Complete AVSD has a common valve and a large nonrestrictive VSD.
added_why_not.Isolated secundum ASD: A secundum ASD has normal AV valves and no inlet VSD.
added_why_not.Partial AVSD without VSD: Partial AVSD has no ventricular-level shunt.
added_why_not.Balloon mitral valvotomy: Balloon mitral valvotomy treats mitral stenosis, not RVOT obstruction.
added_why_not.Pulmonary vein stent: Pulmonary vein stents treat pulmonary vein stenosis.
added_why_not.Atrial septal device closure: Closing the atrial septum would not improve pulmonary blood flow in TOF.
added_why_not.CPS 48 h and PES >72 h: The windows are reversed: CPS uses 72 h and PES evaluates persistence after 48 h.
added_why_not.Both guidelines 24 h: Neither framework uses a single 24-hour window.
